audit_notes: The article describes impacts in separate ward-7 Gara and ward-8 Syala locations. It says the active slide began the previous morning, not on the July 27 publication date.

This is an aggregate Karnali Highway recovery report covering many landslide points across Kalikot/Jumla/Mugu corridors after several days of rain; it does not define one physical event, one district, or one exact event date.
Risk-only story: the Haliya settlement is described as threatened by possible landslides, with no observed dated landslide failure documented.

One article combines two separate failures: a Thursday-morning slide at Gorkha Municipality-11 and a Wednesday-night mudslide at Palungtar Municipality-1. The claimed date/municipality cannot describe both.
The article separately reports the Headbox slide on Thursday evening and the Kerabari slide on Friday morning, so this is more than one physical road failure and not a single July 11 event.
The report states that seven houses were destroyed by landslides across both Raksirang and Kailash rural municipalities, not one physical failure confined to Raksirang.

The landslide impacts are in Nalgad Municipality-3 at Luharkhet and Bangedara, not Bheri Municipality. The source does not safely resolve one-versus-multiple slope failures or an exact occurrence date; the separate river-drowning death is not a landslide death.
The article aggregates a three-kilometre Tila section with 8-10 other landslide sites in Hima/Kanakasundari and additional Mugu sites. It attributes them to rain the previous week, not October 14.
The report refers to plural landslides at Ranibas and only says rainfall had continued since Saturday; it does not establish a single failure or its exact occurrence date.
The report names separate landslides at Mawa Khola, Dati Khola, Panidhara and Ghoptibhir, plus a separate road-collapse point at Nau Kilo.
The article reports separate road-blocking landslides at Aringale Fedi in Kapurkot and Jalekharcha in Bagchaur Municipality, so it is not one failure confined to Kapurkot.
The Khotang death was caused by a person being swept away by a river. Landslide fatalities mentioned in the same story occurred in Ilam, not at the claimed Khotang event.
The story aggregates several landslide-related road blockages around Hetauda/Makwanpur routes, not one Kathmandu landslide. It does not establish a human fatality count for a single event.
The article totals 10 deaths from separate landslides in Dhulikhel, Banepa, Panauti, Namobuddha and Bhumlu rather than one physical failure.

The two same-night reports use different named sites, Ghoptebhir and Nagdi Khola, within Ichchhakamana-4. The evidence is insufficient to prove they are the same physical slide rather than nearby separate failures.
This is a relief follow-up covering landslides at Satyawati-3 Thulo Lumpek and Satyawati-4 Limgha; it reports 13 total deaths but does not state the exact occurrence date.

The article retrospectively describes several different Jaimuni landslides from roughly two years earlier, not a March 2023 event. Two deaths are given for one site, but a total death count across all described failures is not established.

The article documents helicopter evacuation of two maternity patients after broad flood/landslide damage to access infrastructure; it does not identify an individual dated landslide event at Falelung-3.
The named Lumbini Sanskritik Municipality impact is flood/inundation. The article's landslides are in hill districts, not at the claimed Rupandehi municipality event.
Both articles duplicate the same multi-site report, but the report names separate landslides at Khadukhola, Jirikhola, Kalapairakhola and Thulakhet across Nisikhola and Badigad municipalities.
The article refers to plural landslides around Dablyang and only links disruption to rain since Monday evening; it does not safely establish one physical failure or an exact occurrence time.
The follow-up describes landslides across different Marang settlements and states 21 deaths there; the evidence supports multiple physical landslide failures rather than one debris-flow event.
This is a prevention/risk article about possible renewed failure at Krishnabhir and past slope damage; it does not document a new landslide occurring on 2025-04-14.
The article explicitly refers to multiple landslides near Khanibesi that buried temporary shelters and briefly dammed the Budhigandaki, not one physical failure.
The 14 deaths were from an overloaded jeep crash after brake failure in Waling-14; the article does not document a landslide event.
The 11 deaths came from three separate landslides: Pokhara-19, Pokhara-32 and Madi Rural Municipality-11. The row is therefore not one event and is not confined to Pokhara Metropolitan City.
The article gives a nationwide aggregate statistic of more than 300 landslide deaths since January 1, 2020; it does not describe a single Kathmandu landslide event.
The report names separate obstructions near Harre/Babai and Deurali in Surkhet, plus another Dailekh slide; it is not one physical failure.

The report describes slide activity descending from both Balchyung and Kharbari and says it began Friday night and reached the settlement Sunday night; July 2 is the evacuation/reporting day, not the onset date.
The four deaths occurred in two separately named Khaptadchhanna failures: one at Majhigaun and another at Kalukheti.
